en: The *Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Purifying All Eye Diseases*. [Posthumous title of the translator:

Grand Master of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of the State of Su, with a fief of three thousand households, invested with purple robes, posthumously titled Minister of Works, and canonized as Dajian (Great Mirror).

Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān... [translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Temple, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, in accordance with imperial decree].
He resided in the kingdom of Kapilavastu,
in the village of the Śākya clan.
At that time, there was a member of the Śākya clan.
He dwelt in the village of Vālikāvatī,
possessing pure faith in the Buddha, pure faith in the Dharma, and pure faith in the Saṅgha;
he took refuge in the Buddha, took refuge in the Dharma, and took refuge in the Saṅgha.
They have no doubt regarding the Buddha, no doubt regarding the Dharma, and no doubt regarding the Saṃgha;
they devote their whole hearts to the Buddha, their whole hearts to the Dharma, and their whole hearts to the Saṃgha;
they are resolved upon the supreme destination of Perfect Enlightenment.
That person does not perceive the forms and appearances seen by the eye.
At that time, the Śākya Gṛhapati Kṣemaka,
recollecting the Tathāgata, spoke these words:
I prostrate to the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the Wisdom-Torch Dhāraṇī who is able to produce radiance.
I take refuge in the Sugata, the Greatly Compassionate One.
May you protect, mindfully regard, and embrace me, so that my eyes may be purified.
At that time, the World-Honored One, whose ears and eyes transcend those of the world,
heard with his divine ear and saw with his divine eye.
Then the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
Go to the place of the Śākyas;
with this dhāraṇī-mantra, provide protection so as to purify their eyes,
and cause them to be rescued and brought under your care.
May they be nourished and may their boundaries be established;
may their eyes be free from defilement and cataracts, and be liberated from disease.
May this be widely disseminated among the fourfold assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, as well as all other sentient beings.
The mantra is: Tadyathā | hiri miri li kili hīte hūṃ hūṃ huya māṇi hulu hulu nulu nulu svāhā | Ānanda, this is the vidyārāja dhāraṇī.
Regarding the eye-dirt, wind-dirt, jaundice, phlegm, and the three-fold combined diseases:
may my eyes and those of [Name] suffer no pain and shed no tears,
by the true word of the Arhats and the true word of the prohibitions.
By means of the truth of ascetic practice, by means of the truth of the sages,
by means of the truth of dependent origination,
and by means of the truth of suffering and the truth of its origin.
The speech of cessation is true speech;
the speech of the Pratyekabuddhas is true speech.
I, [name], vow that my eyes shall become pure.
The seven Buddhas who have attained equal enlightenment have already spoken it;
I, Śākyamuni, the Arhat and Samyaksaṃbuddha, now speak it.
The Four Great Heavenly Kings have also spoken it, and Śakra, Lord of the Devas, has also spoken it.
The Brahma King, Lord of the Sahā World, also said: "Ānanda,
I do not see anyone in the world of devas, the world of Māras, or among śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas who possesses this Viśuddhanetra Dhāraṇī."
One suffers from cataracts, opacities, and floating halos;
that is to say, it causes the eyes to perceive [beings] as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, or rākṣasīs.
It must be performed by a woman of the Śivī clan;
it may be performed by a kumbhāṇḍa, a female kumbhāṇḍa,
a vetāla, a human practitioner of malevolent incantations, or a brahmin practitioner of malevolent incantations.
None shall dare to transgress it, and none shall fail to respond to its efficacy.
Āyuṣmān Ānanda, you should now receive this dhāraṇī and take it to the village of the Śākyas.
He bestowed the *kṣemaṅka* upon him and delivered my words,
instructing him to recite and maintain this dhāraṇī three times during the day and three times at night.
Ānanda then went there and bestowed the *kṣemaṅka* upon him.
As soon as Kṣemaka heard this dhāraṇī,
his visual channels were purified,
and his eyes attained the sight that is free from all defilements.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Purifying All Eye Diseases.
